The benchmark is highly discriminative in only 3 of 18 assertions. Fifteen assertions pass in both configurations on their single observed run, so most of the suite currently validates baseline Lynx knowledge rather than isolating skill-specific lift.

The clearest skill win is eval 3 (motion-choice): with_skill passed 3/3 while without_skill passed 1/3. The two failing baseline assertions were specifically the Lynx-doc-grounded justification and avoiding generic animation-library advice, so the skill's lift here is about staying anchored to official Lynx UI criteria rather than merely picking `motion-mini`.

Eval 5 (component-family-choice) is the other meaningful separator: with_skill passed 3/3 while without_skill passed 2/3. Both runs compared Popover/Dialog/Sheet correctly, but only the skill-backed run pointed back to official docs or local routing guidance.

Evals 1, 2, 4, and 6 showed no measurable quality lift because both configurations passed all assertions. Those evals may still be useful coverage, but on this iteration they do not distinguish the skill from the baseline.

There is no variance signal yet: each configuration was run only once per eval, and with_skill was a perfect 6/6 while without_skill had two partial failures. The nonzero without_skill stddev in pass_rate comes from differences between evals, not repeated-run flakiness.

The skill improved aggregate pass rate by +0.17 (1.00 vs 0.83), and that gain came entirely from doc-grounding assertions in evals 3 and 5; there were no evals where without_skill outperformed with_skill on any assertion.

Time and token tradeoff is modest but uneven. Aggregate timing slightly favored with_skill (-2.7s mean), but that is driven by eval 1 where with_skill finished much faster (45.6s vs 108.8s); in 4 of 6 evals the skill was actually slower, especially eval 3 (+44.4s) and eval 5 (+9.7s).

Token usage increased with the skill on every eval except official-doc-adoption, for a mean delta of +3,230 tokens. The largest token overheads were component-family-choice (+6,307) and motion-choice (+10,701), matching the two evals where the skill bought more doc-specific reasoning.
